full_text: 1980s computer-aided instruction produced lasting gains in long-term student outcomes.
Interactive whiteboards in 2000s classrooms improved learning outcomes more than equivalent non-digital displays.
The 'flipped classroom' model produces consistent positive learning gains over traditional lectures.
Mueller and Oppenheimer's 2014 finding that handwritten notes outperform laptop notes for conceptual learning has been broadly replicated.
1:1 device programs in K-12 schools have produced meaningful improvements in learning outcomes.
By 2035, AI tutors will have replaced human teachers in most US K-12 classrooms.
By 2040, students taught primarily by AI will outperform peers taught by humans on standardized tests.
By 2035, AI tutors will eliminate the educational achievement gap between high- and low-income US students.
By 2040, the average US student will spend more class time interacting with AI than with human teachers.
By 2035, oral examinations will become the dominant assessment format in US universities due to AI cheating concerns.
